findings.summary: The default amounts don't match the reader's situation, and the big result figure sticks with them. The inputs can be changed, so this is a matter of defaults, not a blocker.
There are too many near-identical funds in the list. The preselected cheapest fund kept the reader from giving up.
Fund tags use jargon with no plain explanation. This is minor next to the main figures.
The fund list's right-hand column shows red minus amounts and ranges that are scary and unclear. The reader can't read a main column. This is the fund list, not the account list in problem 6.
The currency-hedging section is long and technical, and the reader would close the page there. It comes after the main answer, and it doesn't name the colour problem.
The fund fee is shown only as a percentage, not in shekels. The reader wants more detail, and this is not problem 2's gap between options.
The next-best option's '−43 ₪' figure doesn't say whether it is better or worse. That could lead to a wrong choice. Problem 2 is a percentage and problem 10 is the cost line, so neither matches.
